# braze Provider

Manage Braze configuration.

Manage catalogs, catalog items, Content Blocks, email templates, and SDK
Authentication public keys in existing Braze workspaces and apps. Resources and
identity import require Terraform 1.12 or later. Discovery through list resources
and `terraform query` requires Terraform 1.14 or later. There are no data sources.

## Authentication and workspace selection

Set `base_url` to the REST endpoint for your
[Braze instance](https://www.braze.com/docs/api/basics/). Supply a REST API key
through `BRAZE_API_KEY` or `api_key`; an explicit `api_key` overrides the
environment. Empty values are rejected. The endpoint and key must be known before
the provider can contact Braze.

Use the provider configuration for the workspace that owns the objects when
importing or managing them. An import ID or identity alone does not select a
workspace. The REST API key authenticates provider operations; it is distinct
from an app API identifier and from an SDK Authentication RSA public key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.12"
  required_providers {
    braze = { source = "cysp/braze" }
  }
}

provider "braze" {
  # Choose the REST endpoint for your Braze instance.
  base_url = "https://rest.iad-01.braze.com"
  # Set BRAZE_API_KEY in your environment.
}
```

## Resource ownership and deletion

Choose the resource whose ownership matches your workflow. Import an existing
object before managing it, and keep each object in one Terraform state.

| Resource | Ownership and destroy behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `braze_catalog` | Owns the catalog schema. Destroy or replacement deletes the catalog and all items, including items managed elsewhere. |
| `braze_catalog_item` | Owns one item's complete values. Updates remove omitted fields; destroy deletes the item. |
| `braze_content_block` | Owns a Content Block's content and settings. Destroy retains the object in Braze. |
| `braze_email_template` | Owns an email template's content and settings. Destroy retains the template in Braze. |
| `braze_sdk_authentication_key` | Owns one public key. Other keys remain unmanaged. Destroy deletes the key only when it is not primary. |
| `braze_sdk_authentication_keys` | Owns one app's complete key collection. Apply deletes omitted members; destroy retains all keys and relinquishes management. |

Use one SDK Authentication ownership model per app. The collection resource
requires existing keys to be imported first. Both key resources register public
keys only; JWT signing, private-key storage, and SDK Authentication enforcement
remain part of your application setup.

## State and credentials

Use `BRAZE_API_KEY` to keep the REST API key out of configuration. If you pass it
through a Terraform input variable, mark the variable `sensitive` and `ephemeral`
to redact it and omit its value from saved plans and state.

Resource content, catalog values, and public keys are stored in Terraform state.
Account for confidential content when selecting state access controls and
reviewing generated query files. Marking a value sensitive hides normal CLI
output but does not remove it from state; see HashiCorp's
[sensitive data guidance](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/manage-sensitive-data).
Never pass private-key material to `rsa_public_key`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The REST API key to use when communicating with Braze. If not provided, it will default to the value of the BRAZE_API_KEY environment variable.
- `base_url` (String) The absolute REST API URL for your Braze instance, for example https://rest.iad-01.braze.com. This must be set; there is no default instance.

## REST API permissions

Grant the permissions for the operations you use. Creating templates, catalog
items, and SDK authentication keys also requires read permission so the provider
can retrieve the created object. Import and refresh require read permission only.

| Surface | Manage resources | Discovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalogs | `catalogs.create`, `catalogs.get`, `catalogs.delete` | `catalogs.get` |
| Catalog items | `catalogs.create_item`, `catalogs.get_item`, `catalogs.replace_item`, `catalogs.delete_item` | `catalogs.get_items` |
| Content blocks | `content_blocks.create`, `content_blocks.info`, `content_blocks.update` | `content_blocks.list`; also `content_blocks.info` with `include_resource = true` |
| Email templates | `templates.email.create`, `templates.email.info`, `templates.email.update` | `templates.email.list`; also `templates.email.info` with `include_resource = true` |
| SDK authentication keys | `sdk_authentication.create`, `sdk_authentication.keys`, `sdk_authentication.primary`, `sdk_authentication.delete` | Not supported |

See the [catalog endpoints](https://www.braze.com/docs/api/endpoints/catalogs),
[template endpoints](https://www.braze.com/docs/api/endpoints/templates), and
[SDK Authentication endpoints](https://www.braze.com/docs/api/endpoints/sdk_authentication/)
for Braze's permission requirements.
